fullTime.title: Full-time employment
fullTime.text: Full-time, full ownership of a domain. Below the hourly equivalent — that discount buys stability and long-term product ownership.

partTime.title: Part-time
partTime.text: 20–25 hrs/week on fixed days. Fits when you need a strong engineer but not a full-time one.

retainer.title: Support retainer
retainer.text: Agreed hour bank, priority response, security updates. Unused hours roll over one month.

fixedPrice.title: Fixed-price project
fixedPrice.text: Fixed price where scope is well defined. The premium covers uncertainty risk; hourly work carries none.

legacy.why: Time goes to comprehension before change

included.title: What the rate includes
included: Tests for new code, including retry and failure paths
Meaningful commit messages and review turnaround
Deployment, metrics and alerts for what I ship
Fixing my own bugs — free for 30 days
Handover: how it works and why it’s built that way
billed: Meetings beyond one hour per week
Maintaining code I did not write

items.text: Double-entry ledgers, idempotency keys and the outbox pattern: a retried request or a crashed consumer never credits a balance twice.
USDT on TRC-20 and ERC-20, BTC and ETH — confirmation thresholds, reorg handling, hot/cold wallet flows and Fireblocks custody.
Event-driven services on Kafka, RabbitMQ and NATS, load-tested with k6 before a big match or a promo launch sends the traffic.
Kubernetes, Terraform and ArgoCD to ship; Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry and Loki to see what’s happening — the work doesn’t end at merge.

items.strong: Risk and compliance in the flow.
items.text: Fraud and risk scoring and KYC/AML checks sit inside the payment path, not bolted on after launch.
Years of frontend and mobile work mean APIs designed for the clients that consume them — and a back-office UI when the team needs one.

note.text: The lower bound is a well-defined task in a familiar stack. The upper bound is tight deadlines, unfamiliar code, or a high cost of failure. Rates are negotiable: scope, duration and predictability move them more than the category of work does.
